cases.note: Decomposed (2026-07-17): the residual is a proven chaotic-dynamics floor. A type=voltage relay across an open point (monitors 1-phase Transformer.PT3 term2 = Delta.3.2 broken-delta 3V0; switches 3-phase Line.line1), run in dynamics with a t=0.3 s ground fault at Genbus. (1) The relay sizes its per-phase state arrays and VoltageLogic loop by the CONTROLLED element's phase count, `Min(RELAYCONTROLMAXDIM, ControlledElement.NPhases)` = 3, as r4133 does (VoltageLogic, GetPropertyValue 39/40, Sample, Reset), while its own count (1 for the 1-phase PT) drives only vbase/cBuffer/CondOffset. Sized by the relay's own count the loop would read only cBuffer[1] (the 3V0 ~438 V), so Vmag>0 and the relay would trip Line1 (438/277=1.58 pu >> 0.3 pu pickup). With the count of 3 the loop's final phantom phase (beyond the PT terminal's 2 conds) reads 0 so Vmag=0, the `IF Vmag>0` guard fails, OVTime stays -1 and the relay correctly does NOT trip , matching r4133 (state [closed,closed,closed] all 10 steps). relay/mod.rs `state_size` (-> ctrl_snap.nphases), pinned by the relay unit test `voltage_relay_open_point_sizes_state_by_controlled_nphases_59n`. (2) The residual is a chaotic floor: the un-tripped generator (D=1) pole-slips under the sustained fault -- BOTH engines agree (theta 12->777 deg, f 60->79 Hz by t=1.0). Rust matches r4133 to the solver floor with IDENTICAL iteration counts and relay state at every step, and the generator live-f64 state matches to machine-eps early (dTheta 7e-15, dFreq 1.4e-14 at t=0.1). The positive Lyapunov exponent of the pole-slip then amplifies the faer-vs-KLU last-ulp difference EXPONENTIALLY (~2x/step): node-V Linf 4.5e-6 (t=1.1) -> 7.8e-3 (t=1.9) -> O(1 V) by t~2.5, unbounded. The harness checkpoint (deck runs `number=10` inline to t=1.0 during compile, then n_steps>=1 solves -> t>=2.0) necessarily lands in this chaotic regime, where no fixed tolerance honestly BOUNDS the node-V (the t=2.0 value 1.9e-5 is a deterministic chaotic dip, not a floor). A tolerance never masks a gap, so the deck stays parked. The relay sizing is proven against r4133 and unit-gated. Excluded from solvable_now/ad_sweep. Reproducible r4133 probe: `tools/opendss/probe_59n.py` drives this deck on the r4133 engine and checks in both claims -- (A) r4133's own `Relay.State` reads `[closed, closed, closed, ]` (byte-identical to this engine's render, so no-trip is NOT self-pinned) with Line.line1 at ~1381 A, and (B) the generator frequency leaves 60 Hz (~78.9 Hz at t=1.0) and wanders unboundedly (67-115 Hz over 15 s) = pole-slip, no bandable node-V floor. The trajectory above is regenerable with it.

NOT an iteration-count block: measured symmetrically both engines are cold 3 / warm 2 (2026-07-12), the basis on which its Lagging/Leading siblings gate. This deck stays parked for a GENUINE node-V divergence: LineCode.556MCM declares nphases=4 but supplies only a 3x3 (6-entry) cmatrix `(2.849 | -0.922454 3.00287 | -0.353318 -0.587272 2.70828)`. This engine REJECTS the malformed 4-phase Cmatrix ('does not match with the expected order') while dss_capi tolerates it, so the line-charging admittance differs and the 4th-wire/neutral nodes diverge: PRIMARY.4 Rust 13.363452 vs dss_capi 13.363170 (|diff| 2.82e-4), SOURCEBUS.4 13.354755 vs 13.354526, SECONDARY.4/LOADBUS.4 ~2e-5, above the feeder floor. The Lagging/Leading siblings carry a well-formed 4x4 cmatrix and match bit-for-bit. Only this deck's malformed cmatrix triggers the divergence.

SKIPPED-SWEEP re-verified on the newest engines (2026-07-12): still unsolvable everywhere — r3723 NO, r4088 NO, r4133 NO (all diverge, non-convergent at 1000 iters). ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-10: the deck data itself is pathological. The 480 V DER microgrid island (m2001der480-2 delta secondary of a 750 kVA xfmr) is operated at the edge of voltage collapse, and Storage.battery1 (charging)/battery2 (idling) tip the snapshot power flow over the fixed-point stability boundary: |V| at M2001-ESS1 grows geometrically (~x2000/iteration) until NaN. Bisected: both batteries disabled -> converges (121 iters); battery1=discharging -> converges (130); charging or idling -> geometric divergence. Engine-lineage-consistent: pinned oracle, official EPRI r3723/r4088/r4133, and the Rust port all diverge identically on the vendored deck; on the healed variant (storages disabled) Rust converges in EXACTLY the oracle's 121 iterations. Deck/scenario bug, nothing to fix port-side.

Proven cross-solver conditioning floor (decomposition, not a tolerance sweep, re-affirmed 2026-07-12). cond(assembled Y) = 9.79e11, driven by two linecode-BUSBAR ultra-switch lines in series with the 46 kV source: Line.MDV_SUB_1_HSB (length=0.001 units=m -> ~1e-10 ohm -> Y~1e10 S; the dominant ill-conditioner) and Line.SSswitch (~1e-7 ohm -> Y~1e7 S). The step-0 entry-0 node-V |diff|=5.53e-1 (rel 2.08e-5) at BUSSOURCE/MDV_SUB_1_HSB is solver junk in the ill-conditioned direction. Decomposition: assembled Y BIT-IDENTICAL (570/570 entries max|dY|=0); Vsource injection Yprim*E BIT-IDENTICAL; loads identical to 7 figs; on the equivalent linear system the three solvers spread comparably — faer(Rust) vs KLU(OpenDSS) 0.758 V, faer vs scipy(equilibrated) 0.555 V, KLU vs scipy 0.776 V — residual parity ||Y*V-inj||inf 4.40e-2 (Rust) vs 4.56e-2 (OpenDSS); neither engine is more correct. Regulator lands the identical tap; the 0.55 V gap is IDENTICAL with the regulator disabled (RegControl+SubXfmr exonerated). A ~1 V v_abs band (~4e-5 rel at 46 kV) is too wide to admit without masking real substation-transformer bugs, so it stays documented here (floating_zeroseq_bus precedent).

An INTENTIONAL r4133 change, NOT an OpenDSS bug: the original stays unsolvable under r4133 by design, and equivalent coverage is gated via twins. Evidence: the 11.0.0.1 release notes announce the protection overhaul explicitly ('Added RatedCurrent property to ... Fuses', 'Standardized TCC curve behavior - no curves assigned by default'). The r4133 Fuse property help says 'Multiplying the current values in the curve by the CurveMultiplier value gives the actual current' and calls RatedCurrent 'Not used internally for either power flow or reporting'. The COM ridl exposes CurveMultiplier with matching helpstrings. The same RatedCurrent=nameplate/InterruptingRating pattern is applied across Fuse/Recloser/Relay/SwtControl, and r4133 keeps a compat alias where intended (Recloser prop 37 PhaseTrip -> PhFastPickup+PhSlowPickup) but repurposes Fuse prop 6 with no fallback. EPRI ships this example un-migrated in the r4133 trunk (still RatedCurrent=65): example maintenance, not an engine defect. Physics: Fuse.f2 (Tlink, monitors Transformer.Tg t1) carries 52.2-53.5 A of steady motor load (controls-off snapshot, all engines bit-similar). Old semantics 53.5/65=0.82x < 2.0x min-melt -> holds (a 65 A link at 0.83x rating does not melt). r4133 default divisor 1.0 -> 53.5x > Tlink last point 50x -> clamps to 0.02 s -> blows all 3 phases at Sec=0 (eventlog 'Fuse.f2 PHASE 1/2/3 BLOWN'), islanding Tg + IndMach012.Motor1 -> non-convergence (r4133 26 iters NO; r4088 + dss_capi 0.14.5 converge 18 iters, digit-identical). This engine follows r4133 (reproduces the non-convergence). EQUIVALENT COVERAGE: single-edit twins (CurveMultiplier=65 restores the coordination) live-gated vs r4133 in controls/fuse/indmach_r4133/{indmach_snap,indmach_dyn}.dss, the snapshot surface here, the full Run.dss dynamics surface in indmach_dyn. Applies to Master.DSS and its Run.dss driver.

An INTENTIONAL r4133 change, NOT an OpenDSS bug: see the Master.DSS entry above for the evidence (release notes, the Fuse property help, the COM ridl, cross-class consistency, the no-fallback repurpose of prop 6). This driver adds the dynamics surface: on r4088/0.14.5 the snapshot converges (18 iters), then the 5001-step dynamics run applies the SLG fault at t=0.3 s, Relay.mfrov/uv isolates the motor ~0.42 s, Recloser.rec1 trips FAST at Sec=0.5115, the temporary fault clears, both fuses hold, motor coasts down to f=57.2053 Hz. On r4133 the snapshot already fails (Fuse.f2 blown at Sec=0) so the dynamics never start. EQUIVALENT COVERAGE: controls/fuse/indmach_r4133/indmach_dyn.dss (engines r4133) reproduces this exact sequence under r4133 semantics via the single edit CurveMultiplier=65, probe-proven identical protection ops and end-state motor f64 vars to ~6 sig digits vs the r4088 original. Gated with full-model per-step + monitors (7 monitors x 5001 samples) + fuse/relay/recloser state probes + IndMach012 variables + eventlog + ctrlqueue.
